title: Bitoshi Nakamoto
type: Adventurer · loyalty, grief and chosen bonds
dek: An explorer who came looking for Jiangshi and built a life with her and Adelia, through awkward courtship, failed assumptions, repeated loss, searching and practical care.

profile.personality: Bitoshi offers companionship without requiring grief to end first. His hope accepts uncertainty, while loyalty can make his judgment of retreat or betrayal severe.
profile.achievements: His early explorations connect Prima, The Before and Gael. He lives through Jiangshi’s absence, encounters her memorial and later witnesses her return, preserving the significance of both loss and recovery.
profile.relationships: Adelia and Jiangshi are central to his chosen bonds. Alyhotep is remembered as an old friend. His anger at Nienna’s retreat preserves a grieving companion’s perspective rather than a settled judgment of the tactical choice.

body:
Bitoshi Nakamoto arrives looking for Jiangshi, then finds himself trying to understand both Adelia’s love and his own. Away from those intimate conversations, he scouts, steadies ropes, carries supplies and helps the wounded. The same person can be formal, embarrassed, tender and harsh when he believes someone has abandoned a friend.

Scouting, rope and the dangerous valley

Bitoshi joins the early exploration of Prima, The Before and Gael. He helps reopen roads, survives the mountain storm and undead valley, explores the buried city and witnesses the Flying Horror’s escape. His history includes useful work and dangerous investigation beyond his closest relationships.

His fieldwork gives that history practical detail. In the buried passages he keeps high, scouts from cover and uses his owl to help investigate. In the mountain expedition he offers rope, tethers himself to steady others and calls on the ancestors for guidance.

A later crossing finds him still marked by the rock slide and explaining that he has learned to keep farther from an edge. He can offer a safer method because an earlier mistake hurt him. As Quake’s shade falls in the valley, Bitoshi rushes to his companions and squeezes healing berries into their mouths. The narrator confirms that everyone is up again. He then gathers bones and armor and helps the company toward safety.

His remarks about darkness are similarly grounded in what he can use. Shadows may hide and protect people, he argues. In the ruins he also finds darkness that his sight cannot penetrate and asks Adelia what she can see. Comfort with shadow does not make every dark place familiar.

Jiangshi’s absence and return

Jiangshi’s loss brings Bitoshi into conflict with Nienna’s retreat. He and Adelia experience it as abandonment; Gartina argues that returning would probably have created another unrecoverable death. The surviving accounts preserve their disagreement without establishing that grief makes one tactical assessment universally correct.

During the absence, Bitoshi searches for Jiangshi and encounters a memorial. Later she is alive beside him again. Her return changes the present without making the memorial, the search or the intervening grief unreal.

The recovered scenes distinguish a return in the Month of Cala, Year 1 from the new loss during the assault on Wrath. At the earlier reunion, Bitoshi reaches for Jiangshi’s hand, helps bring her with the company and thinks about feeding her Gartina’s cooking. He has the person beside him again, not only a dream or memorial.

After Wrath, he asks Death to give Jiangshi back and offers his shield alongside the others’ possessions. Death refuses the exchange; Bitoshi takes the shield up again and carries Adelia. He later searches the lava fields with magic, hoping surviving belongings will lead him to remains.

His anger does not exclude his own part in what happened. In a later conversation with Adelia he lists things that others might have done differently, then admits that he could have arrived sooner. Those are his judgments after seeing the replayed events, not a finding that any one companion caused every loss.

Hope without a promise

Accounts of the loss describe Bitoshi holding and consoling Adelia, then proposing prayer for Jiangshi’s return or safety beyond their reach. He does not promise that a miracle must follow. When Adelia doubts the gods, he asks whether hope must also be surrendered.

His repeated image of three strands expresses the strength he finds with Adelia and Jiangshi. He describes the strength they find in staying together. Their later family language is preserved below, while the complete relationship chronology remains open.

Loyalty and its hard edge

Support does not make Bitoshi endlessly gentle. His loyalty can become severe when he sees survival as abandonment or another person’s trust being betrayed. The public record establishes his anger and care; it does not establish every later confrontation or resolve every disputed judgment.

The account also preserves his criticism of Fein Uaill’s prestige and possessions as a form of confinement. This remains Bitoshi’s assessment of the city, rather than a neutral description of every resident.

The open record

Bitoshi gives an account of his life before arrival, his training and his half-death, but the full biography and magical process remain incompletely recovered. The record distinguishes multiple losses and returns; a later living appearance does not supply the mechanism for every return.

His declarations of love, response to Adelia’s proposal and later description of Jiangshi as a wife are preserved, while the complete marriage chronology and formal terms remain open. His full history with Alyhotep and later outcomes are also incomplete. Sharing a player with another adventurer does not make the characters one person. His relational importance is not an inferred measure of world-scale power.

Gael: helping continuity become a place

In the July 2026 Tower conversation, Bitoshi helps with the sanctuary area for the Place of Recall while Jiangshi resets the small sanctuary she and Adelia had made. The scene gives his relational role a practical form: support for people becomes work on somewhere they can return.

The company also discusses future prayer, meditation and buildings near Hope. His assistance is recorded; a completed temple and full site plan are not. Gael’s later restoration history keeps that work beside the earlier expedition’s losses and care.

A classmate he has come to find

At the Gate, Bitoshi tells Gartina that he has come to find Jiangshi, a classmate and family friend. He has seen a shared dream or nightmare and does not yet know whether she is with the ancestors or may still be reached. The formal bow cannot keep every feeling out of the conversation.

He describes himself as new to a state of half-death and says his people sustain him with magical berries. In later conversations he says the change was part of his mission to bring Jiangshi back. These are his accounts of his own condition and purpose; they do not independently establish all the magic involved.

When Adelia mentions Jiangshi in the tavern, he reacts before he can recover his composure. Tea, questions about obligations and memories of their schooldays follow. He eventually admits that Jiangshi was his first schoolboy crush. The search involves someone he knew before arriving, and his early efforts to speak with Adelia are awkward as well as dutiful.

Learning to ask what Adelia wants

The early relationship is not a seamless agreement among three people. Bitoshi believes Jiangshi has chosen Adelia and that he should withdraw. He takes comfort with Daffodil, misunderstands Adelia’s letter and later recognizes that his assumptions have hurt her.

At Eovar Harbor he apologizes. He admits that he had treated Jiangshi’s wishes as decisive without understanding that Adelia had wishes of her own. He asks whether he may still accompany her to recover Jiangshi, whether or not she returns his affection, and tells her that he loves them both.

When Adelia offers another chance, his first response is joy; then he stops himself long enough to say that he must speak with Daffodil too. The scene leaves him responsible for more than one person’s feelings. His later language of an unbroken bond comes after a misunderstanding that required an apology.

Searching after the others have gone home

With Adelia and later Wren, Bitoshi keeps looking after the battle. He proposes a place for prayer, tries to detect surviving magic beneath the lava and says news should reach the people in Pristinia who cared for the fallen. He wants Wren found too, remembering that she organized an earlier commemoration when she scarcely knew them.

By the Month of Hope, Year 1, he is tired and frustrated. The search finally turns up a surviving piece of Olokun’s belongings, protected beneath rock. Bitoshi recognizes it, digs and insists that the discovery was something they did together. It gives him renewed hope; it is not Jiangshi’s recovered body or a completed resurrection.

When Adelia questions the gods and the value of waiting, he does not promise a miracle. He asks whether he should give up hope and whether she would give up on Jiangshi or on him. He believes their ancestors may still help. He also believes others have too readily accepted the dead remaining gone, a judgment that reveals his grief without deciding what every companion actually felt or tried.

Three strands, and the work of staying

Later scenes find Jiangshi beside Bitoshi and Adelia again. He speaks of their bond as three strands that are difficult to break. At the castle he agrees to Adelia’s proposal, and a later quest entrance calls Jiangshi one of his wives. These are stronger indications of the family they describe than the earlier uncertainty, while leaving the ceremony, full terms and complete chronology unrecovered.

He remains severe when he thinks their care has been betrayed. His description of Fein Uaill as a gilded cage belongs to him, as do his criticisms of the city’s prestige, possessions and restrictions. The profile preserves those views without making every resident share the same motives.

When Hope needs renewal, he travels with the company, asks whether another spell or divine intervention might help and continues to support Adelia. He later plans to defend the site and helps prepare the sanctuary for a Place of Recall. Helpers, meals, watchkeeping and carrying equipment give him work to do while greater magical questions remain open.

At Papirak’s funeral, he arrives with Jiangshi and Adelia’s projection, moves with the procession and stays beside Pappy. He accepts a white flower, recalls the mentorship he received and puts a hand on his grieving friend’s shoulder. He and his family stay close while giving Pappy room. The history that began with looking for a lost classmate has room for another person’s grief too.
